source_refs.note: Exercise 9.2, Question 11 (book page 273); the book prints no answers for Exercise 9.2; answers checked with sympy and the solution book

blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein har term ek trigonometric function hai jis ke andar inverse trigonometric function baitha hai, jaise \(\tan^2\) ke andar \(\sec^{-1} 3\).
Diya kya hai? Sirf do numbers: 3 aur 4. Sabit kya karna hai? Ke dono squares ka jama 23 hai.
Trick yeh hai ke inverse function ko ek angle ka naam de dein; phir sawal seedha trigonometry ka ban jata hai.
Rule kaunsa? Pythagorean identities \(1 + \tan^2\alpha = \sec^2\alpha\) aur \(1 + \cot^2\beta = \csc^2\beta\), kyunke yeh wohi do functions jorti hain jo humein chahiye.
Plan: angle ka naam, identity, value, aur aakhir mein jama.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(\tan^2(\sec^{-1} 3) + \cot^2(\csc^{-1} 4)\).
Saabit karna hai: yeh 23 ke barabar hai.
Tareeqa: \(\alpha = \sec^{-1} 3\) aur \(\beta = \csc^{-1} 4\) rakhenge, bilkul waise jaise kitab Example 8 mein inverse function ko angle ka naam deti hai. Phir \(1 + \tan^2\alpha = \sec^2\alpha\) aur \(1 + \cot^2\beta = \csc^2\beta\) lagayenge. Yeh identities isliye chuni hain ke pehli mein sec (jo maloom hai) aur tan (jo chahiye) dono hain, aur doosri mein csc (maloom) aur cot (chahiye) dono hain.

Pehle angle ka naam rakhein
\[\alpha = \sec^{-1} 3\]
\[\sec\alpha = 3\]
Kyun: \(y = \sec^{-1} x\) ka matlab hi yeh hai ke \(\sec y = x\); yani \(\sec^{-1} 3\) woh angle hai jiska sec 3 hai. 3 domain mein hai kyunke \(\sec^{-1}\) sirf un numbers ke liye defined hai jin ka \(|x| \ge 1\) ho, aur \(|3| = 3 \ge 1\).

\(\tan^2\alpha\) nikalein
\[\tan^2\alpha = \sec^2\alpha - 1\]
\[= 3^2 - 1 = 8\]
Kyun: Identity \(1 + \tan^2\alpha = \sec^2\alpha\) mein se 1 doosri taraf le gaye. Achhi baat yeh hai ke sawal mein square hai, is liye humein yeh faisla hi nahi karna ke \(\tan\alpha\) \(+\sqrt{8}\) hai ya \(-\sqrt{8}\); square dono ka 8 hi hai.
Dhyan dein: \(\sec^2\alpha = 3^2 = 9\) hai, 6 nahi; square ka matlab number ko khud se multiply karna hai.

Doosre angle ka naam rakhein
\[\beta = \csc^{-1} 4\]
\[\csc\beta = 4\]
Kyun: Wohi definition: \(y = \csc^{-1} x\) ka matlab \(\csc y = x\). 4 bhi domain mein hai kyunke \(|4| \ge 1\).

\(\cot^2\beta\) nikalein
\[\cot^2\beta = \csc^2\beta - 1\]
\[= 4^2 - 1 = 15\]
Kyun: Identity \(1 + \cot^2\beta = \csc^2\beta\) se. Yeh pehli identity ki "jurwan behan" hai: wahan tan aur sec the, yahan cot aur csc hain.

Ab jama karein
\[\text{L.H.S} = \tan^2\alpha + \cot^2\beta\]
\[= 8 + 15 = 23\]
\[= \text{R.H.S}\]
Kyun: Sawal ka left side bilkul \(\tan^2\alpha + \cot^2\beta\) hi hai, kyunke \(\alpha\) aur \(\beta\) hum ne inhi inverse functions ke naam rakhe the. Dono values rakh di, aur right side 23 aa gaya.

Tasdeeq: right triangles se
\[\sec\alpha = 3:\ \text{adj} = 1,\ \text{hyp} = 3\]
\[\text{opp} = \sqrt{9 - 1} = \sqrt{8}\]
\[\csc\beta = 4:\ \text{opp} = 1,\ \text{hyp} = 4\]
\[\text{adj} = \sqrt{16 - 1} = \sqrt{15}\]
Kyun: \(\sec = \text{hyp}/\text{adj}\), is liye \(\sec\alpha = 3\) wala triangle hypotenuse 3 aur adjacent 1 ka hai; Pythagoras se opposite \(\sqrt{8}\). Isi tarah \(\csc = \text{hyp}/\text{opp}\) se doosra triangle. Figure dekhiye: \(\tan^2\alpha = (\sqrt{8}/1)^2 = 8\) aur \(\cot^2\beta = (\sqrt{15}/1)^2 = 15\). Dono raaste ek hi jawab dete hain.

answer_figure.alt: Two right triangles. Left: angle alpha, adjacent side 1, hypotenuse 3, opposite side root 8, so sec alpha = 3 and tan squared alpha = 8. Right: angle beta, opposite side 1, hypotenuse 4, adjacent side root 15, so csc beta = 4 and cot squared beta = 15.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Kitab mein Exercise 9.2 ke jawab chhape hue nahi hain. Is page ka har hal hamara apna hai: qadam ba qadam kiya gaya, computer algebra system (sympy) se alag se check kiya gaya, aur ek solution book se bhi milaya gaya. Is liye aap apna proof yahan wale proof se mila kar dekh sakte hain; agar aap ka tareeqa alag hai magar har qadam ki wajah sahi hai, to woh bhi theek hai.
